# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S3 Add parseISO to the ms library as the inverse of formatISO, so that parseISO("PT1H30M") returns 5400000, with exports and tests (continuing the ISO 8601 duration work) (Nov 3, 9:19 AM)
**Investigated**: Reviewed src/index.ts at HEAD 4dd911d, which had formatISO but no ISO parser, and found that the existing parse() regex handles only single value-unit strings. Read src/format-iso.test.ts to confirm the output contract that parseISO must invert, including PT0S for zero, P1D for whole days, and P1DT1H1M1S. Checked jest.config.ts, which enforces 100% global coverage.

**Learned**: formatISO's output format defines the grammar parseISO must accept: a P designator, an optional T section, and time components H, M and S, with days as the largest unit. Parsing has to reject years and months because their lengths are ambiguous. The test suite and coverage threshold require every new branch to be exercised.

**Completed**: parseISO was added to src/index.ts and exported. It accepts weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds, an optional leading + or - sign, fractional seconds with either . or , as the separator, and case-insensitive input. It returns NaN for years, months and malformed strings, and throws for empty, overlong or non-string input. The result is rounded to the nearest millisecond. src/parse-iso.test.ts was created with tests for these cases plus a round-trip through formatISO. The full Jest run passes 187 of 187 tests with 100% coverage, and tsc is clean. A Biome lint warning about string concatenation in the test file was fixed by switching to a template literal, and Biome now reports no issues. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: Commit the parseISO change and its tests on the current branch, following the commit style of the previous formatISO commit. Decide whether to keep weeks support, since formatISO never emits weeks, and whether NaN for invalid strings should stay consistent with parse().

**Notes**: Two design choices may need the user's sign-off: accepting P2W even though formatISO never produces weeks, and returning NaN rather than throwing on malformed strings to match parse(). The branch state should be checked before committing, since earlier parseCompound work lives on feat/parse-compound and formatISO was committed as 4dd911d.
